title: Mage hotfix (70685): Fire/Arcane talents reshuffled, Accelerant, Precision, Arcane Focus removed, Ice Lance r1 8 s CD
claim: The build 70685 hotfix data changes Mage talents: Improved Fireball becomes Accelerant (5 ranks, -0.1 to -0.5 s cast on Fireball, Frostfire Bolt and Arcane Wrath); Elemental Precision becomes Precision (3 ranks, +2/4/6% hit with all spells); Critical Mass drops to 3 ranks (2/4/6% Fire crit, was 5 ranks); Incineration rises to 5 ranks (2-10% crit on Fire Blast, Ice Lance, Arcane Blast, Scorch, was 3); Arcane Focus is removed; Ice Lance rank 1 gets an 8 s cooldown.
detail: Unannounced; no patch note. Two independent extractions: wowsims read the raidbots 'forever' hotfix cache (build 70685, push 113441; tree sizes now 18/17/18, every Mage preset had to be remapped), and seos-a/forever-info's sync of Wowhead's Forever data on Oct 29 shows the same ranks and texts. Client tables for 70685 changed only 3 rows (daybreakforever), so this ships as a server hotfix. Leveling impact: a Frost or Fire leveler must re-plan talents (Precision now covers Arcane too; old builds with Arcane Focus or 5/5 Critical Mass are illegal). Ice Lance rank 1 (1312002) has the cooldown, rank 6 (1240047) has none per wowsims: check whether the low ranks you level with are on cooldown. Other classes, racials and items unchanged in this push.

title: Mage: Frost Blast (all 3 ranks) removed from the 70685 hotfix data
claim: The wowsims ingestion of the build 70685 hotfix cache lists Frost Blast spells 1326053, 1326054 and 1326055 (ranks 1-3, the level 24/36/48 AoE slow) as removed, and wowsims deleted Frost Blast from its Mage sim.
detail: Single source so far. Wowhead's talent tooltips (via forever-info) still name Frost Blast in Improved Frostbolt, Arctic Reach, Winter's Chill and Missile Barrage, so the removal may be incomplete or the tooltips stale. If live, Frost Mages lose the level-24 kiting/AoE tool from n:20261017-mage-frost-blast-24 (and n:20261024-frost-blast-coefficient-cut no longer matters). Check the trainer at 24 on day 1 before planning Frost AoE routes around it.

detail: Daybreak's per-build diff names the rows but not the new tent text or category values. The Mage and Hunter number changes on this build were server hotfixes (n:20261029-mage-talent-hotfix-70685, n:20261028-hunter-hawk-trueshot-70658).

title: Hunter hotfix: Aspect of the Hawk ranks 1-6 give much less RAP (15/22/30/38/47/55); Trueshot Aura 15/22/30/40
claim: Since an Oct 28 server hotfix on the launch realms, Aspect of the Hawk gives ranged attack power R1 15, R2 22, R3 30, R4 38, R5 47, R6 55 (was 20/35/50/70/90; Classic R6 110; rank 7 stays 120) and Trueshot Aura ranks give 15/22/30/40 (was 30/40/50/75).
detail: Unannounced; no patch note. ForeverChanges reads it as a hotfix served by the launch realms on Oct 28; ForeverDB, WCLBox and forever-info's Wowhead sync (build 70685) show the same values; a US forum thread (Oct 28) lists them too. Same diff: Hunter's Mark rank 4 RAP 71->143, the Explosive Trap Effect spell removed (traps scale with AP), Survivalist's Discipline proc no longer 100%. Lowers early Hunter ranged DPS while leveling: re-check modeled Hunter kill times. Check the Hawk tooltip at 10.

title: Tauren Plainsrunning stacks drop when you stop, talk to NPCs or take a hit
claim: Players report that Plainsrunning stacks fall off or reset while an NPC/quest dialog is open or when you stop to gather or kill, and that one hit roughly halves the stacks; a full 60% stack takes about a minute of uninterrupted running.
detail: US forum (Sangrin, Oct 28) on quest dialogs; EU thread 'Plainsrunning confusion' (Oct 27-29, BronzATwrk, MrTeddy, Wubear): stopping to gather, kill or talk drastically reduces or resets stacks, one hit about halves them, 2% per tick up to 60%, no benefit mounted, works indoors. No staff reply. Route advice: accept/turn in fast, avoid pulls while traveling, and treat Plainsrunning as travel-only speed between hubs (n:20261027-plainsrunning-60pct-on-foot). Verify the build-up time on day 1.

title: Launch layering: each zone or zone group is its own layer
claim: Blizzard says each zone or zone group is its own layer at launch, with connected zones such as Durotar and Orgrimmar sharing servers, which fixes the beta's players popping in and out at zone borders.
detail: WoW: Forever Podcast episode 6 (Oct 29; Aggrend, principal engineer Frank Williams, lead engineer Ana Resendez). Blizzard chooses which zones connect; groupings are expected to change after launch when city battles begin. During the beta a per-zone cap in Westfall and The Barrens was halved, which fixed overcrowding within a day or two. Greenfield: Forever will never be a perfect continuous world, so you can still hit a zone boundary or need a World Refresh. For routes: expect a fresh layer (different mob and node state) when crossing into a zone group, and keep groups together across borders. Related: n:20261020-layer-swap-group-zone-border, n:20261026-layering-transport-capital-fix, n:20261013-world-refresh-layer-switch.
